title: Feeling of Knowing in Large Language Models
claim: A specific internal signal emerges abruptly in late layers rather than early ones, consistently across model scales under causal intervention.
layout: 2 panels side by side; heatmap left, line plot right with shaded layer-region bands
description: Two-panel empirical figure. Panel (a) is a causal-tracing heatmap for a single factual question ("Of which African country is Niamey the capital?") on Qwen2.5-7B. Layers L0–L24 run on the y-axis and input tokens on the x-axis. Tokens are grouped by colored header bars: Prompt, Question, Template. A purple-to-yellow colorbar shows FoK signal strength. A red dashed line marks the FoK layers, and a callout points to a bright yellow hotspot at the late-layer question tokens and the final template token. Panel (b) is a line plot of FoK signal strength against normalized layer depth (0–100%) for Qwen2.5 sizes 0.5b to 32b. A blue band marks Knowledge Layers and a green band marks FoK Layers. Most curves jump sharply in the green band. The eye goes first to the heatmap hotspot.
caption: FoK signal localizes late under causal restoration. Panel (a) shows a 7B example across tokens and layers; panel (b) aggregates FoK recovery across Qwen2.5 sizes over normalized depth.
abstract: Post-training updates change what large language models (LLMs) can answer, but may leave their answerability judgments misaligned. We study this knowledge-judgment desynchronization through functional feeling of knowing (FoK), which supports selective generation, retrieval triggering, and model routing without implying subjective experience. We propose two trainable channels: a knowledge channel that changes answerability and a FoK channel that judges the current knowledge state. Three stages train them: on-policy supervised fine-tuning (OP-SFT) updates knowledge from corrected on-policy answers; knowledge-delta FoK training (K$Î$-FT) adapts judgments across intermediate knowledge states; and FoK-guided policy optimization (FGPO) trains the subsequent answer or explanation. Factual-QA experiments, cross-dataset evaluation, and three sequential updates show that explicit FoK alignment improves judgment quality on updated knowledge. MMLU and ARC-Easy separately assess capability preservation.
